title: Fix crash when attaching more than 10 photos to an inspection
body:
## Problem
The app closes without warning when a technician adds the 11th photo to an inspection on a phone with 3 GB of memory. Two customers reported it in September.

## Acceptance criteria
- [x] Adding photos up to the app's limit does not crash on the two lowest-memory test phones.
- [x] Thumbnails are made at a reduced size and released when the screen closes.
- [x] Memory use stays flat while photos are added, checked with the profiler on one iPhone and one Android phone.
- [x] A regression test adds 12 photos in a row.
notes:
## What changed
Photos were decoded at full size to make thumbnails. Thumbnails are now made from a downscaled copy and the full image is released straight away.

## How it was checked
Profiler run on one iPhone and one Android phone; memory stayed flat. The regression test is in the pull request.

## Follow-ups
Retrying failed uploads is a separate ticket (#5).

title: Send a push notification when a job is assigned
body:
## Why
Technicians learn about a new job only when they open the app. A push notification gets the job to them within seconds, which is what dispatchers keep asking for.

## Acceptance criteria
- [x] Assigning a job sends one push notification to the assigned technician on iOS and on Android.
- [x] Tapping the notification opens that job.
- [x] A retry after a network error never sends the same notification twice.
- [x] The vendor is called through one module so it can be replaced (see ADR-0002).
- [x] Technicians can switch assignment notifications off in the app settings.
notes:
## What changed
The server sends a notification when the assignee of a job changes. The notification carries the job id and nothing else; the title and text are filled in on the phone.

## Decisions
The job id and the assignee form the idempotency key, so a retry is a no-op for the vendor.

## Not done
A daily summary notification is out of scope.

title: Show a sync status banner on the job list
body:
## Why
Technicians cannot tell whether the list in front of them is fresh. A banner should say when the list was last updated, and when the phone has no connection.

## Acceptance criteria
- [x] The banner reads "Updated just now", "Updating" or "No connection, showing the list from <time>".
- [x] The banner does not push the list down when it appears.
- [x] The text is readable in the light and dark system themes and is read out by the screen reader.
notes:
## What changed
A small banner above the job list, driven by the last successful sync time and the connection state. It overlays the top of the list instead of pushing it.

## How it was checked
Tried with the connection switched off in the middle of a sync, on one iPhone and one Android phone, in both themes.

title: Capture a customer signature on the completion screen
body:
## Why
Customers sign a paper form at the end of an inspection today. We want the signature inside the inspection record.

## Acceptance criteria
- [x] The completion screen has a signature box the customer can sign with a finger.
- [x] A cleared signature can be redrawn.
- [x] The signature is saved as an image attached to the inspection and shown in the report.
- [ ] The box works on a small screen (320 points wide) without the keyboard covering it.
- [x] The complete button stays disabled until a signature exists, for jobs that need one.
notes:
## State of the work
The signature box, redraw and saving are done and tested on two large phones.

## Not yet checked
The small-screen case. I have not tried a 320-point screen, so I do not know whether the keyboard covers the box. A reviewer with a small phone, please try it.

title: Retry failed photo uploads with exponential backoff
body:
## Why
When a photo upload fails on a weak connection the technician has to attach the photo again. Uploads should retry by themselves.

## Acceptance criteria
- [x] A failed upload is retried up to 5 times, with the delay doubling from 2 seconds.
- [x] Errors that retrying cannot fix (rejected file, no permission) are not retried.
- [x] After the last failed retry the photo stays in the upload queue and is marked as waiting.
- [x] The inspection shows how many photos are still waiting.
- [x] Unit tests cover the delay sequence and the errors that are not retried.
notes:
## State of the work
All five criteria are met and the unit tests pass. I tested by switching the phone to airplane mode in the middle of an upload on one iPhone and one Android phone.

## Notes for the reviewer
The retry timing is in one file, so the numbers are easy to change after the pilot.

title: Add Vietnamese translation for checklist screens
body:
## Why
One of our prospects has technicians who work in Vietnamese. Checklists are the screens they use all day.

## Acceptance criteria
- [x] Every string on the checklist screens exists in the Vietnamese language file.
- [x] Dates and numbers follow Vietnamese conventions.
- [x] The app falls back to English for any string that is missing.
- [ ] A native speaker has reviewed the wording of the checklist screens.
notes:
## State of the work
The strings and formats are in. The translator sent a first draft on 8 October.

## Not done
The wording has not been reviewed by a native speaker yet.

title: Offline sync: operation log and batch upload
body:
## Why
Technicians lose time and trust when the app needs a signal. ADR-0001 sets the design. This ticket builds the server side and connects the phone's queue to it.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The server accepts uploaded operations in batches and applies them in order.
- [ ] An operation log is kept on the server for the period set in ADR-0001.
- [ ] Conflicting edits to the same field follow the rule in ADR-0001.
- [ ] Uploading the same batch twice changes nothing.
- [ ] A phone with a wrong clock cannot overwrite newer work.
- [ ] The feature sits behind a server-side flag, so a pilot group can be switched on and off without a release.
- [ ] Tests cover clock skew, duplicate uploads and a phone that stays offline for several days.
notes:
## State of the work
The operation log table and the batch upload endpoint are done. The client queue is being connected to them.

## Problem
Two conflict-rule tests fail when two edits arrive in the same second. I am finding out whether this is a bug or a gap in the design.

title: Barcode scanning for equipment tags
body:
## Why
Technicians type equipment tag numbers by hand today, and typos send inspections to the wrong machine. Two customers asked for scanning.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The app scans one-dimensional barcodes and QR codes from equipment tags.
- [ ] A scanned tag opens the equipment record; an unknown tag offers manual entry.
- [ ] A torch button helps in dark plant rooms.
- [ ] Scanning works on the oldest Android phone we support, with a focus time under 2 seconds.
- [ ] Camera permission is asked for only when the scanner opens, with a plain explanation.
notes:
## State of the work
Scanning works on both test phones. The camera permission flow is done.

## Problem
The oldest Android phone is slow to focus. Trying continuous autofocus.

title: Filters on the job list: status, site and date
body:
## Why
Dispatchers assign many jobs to one technician, and the list gets long. Technicians want to see today's jobs at a site, or only the ones that are not finished.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The list can be filtered by status, site and date.
- [ ] Active filters are shown as chips that can be removed one by one.
- [ ] The chosen filters are remembered when the app is reopened.
- [ ] The empty state says which filter hides the jobs and offers to clear it.
notes:
## State of the work
Just started. The status filter is working in a prototype.

title: Draft the pilot success criteria for Harbourline
body:
## Why
A pilot without agreed measures ends in an argument about whether it worked. We want Harbourline's contact and us to agree, before the start, on what we will measure.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The draft lists the measures and a target for each.
- [ ] For each measure it says where the number comes from.
- [ ] Ines has read it.
- [ ] It has been sent to Harbourline's named contact.
notes:
## State of the work
First draft in progress. This is a document ticket: there is no code, so this file is where the work lives.

## Open
I still need a baseline for how many inspections a technician finishes a day on paper.

title: Dark mode for inspection screens
body:
## Why
Some technicians work in dark rooms and prefer a dark screen. It came up in feedback but was not asked for by any pilot candidate, so it waits.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Every inspection screen has a dark variant that follows the phone's setting.
- [ ] Photos, signatures and report previews are readable in both themes.
- [ ] Contrast meets the accessibility guidelines in both themes.

title: Export an inspection report as PDF
body:
## Why
Customers want to attach a finished inspection to their own records and to email it to their own customers.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A finished inspection can be exported as one PDF.
- [ ] The PDF shows the checklist answers, photos and signature in the order of the inspection.
- [ ] The file name contains the job number and the date.
- [ ] A long inspection with many photos still produces a PDF that opens on a phone.

title: Alert before the sync gateway certificate expires
body:
## Why
This is an action item from the postmortem of the September sync outage. The certificate expired without any warning, and we found out from a customer.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] An alert fires 21 days before the certificate expires.
- [ ] A second alert fires at 7 days and a third at 1 day.
- [ ] The alert pages the on-call engineer and links to the incident runbook.
- [ ] The alert is tested in staging with a certificate that expires soon.

title: Move shared API keys into the secret manager and rotate them
body:
## Why
A few keys are still shared in team password notes. The security basics say secrets live in the secret manager and are rotated regularly.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A list of every key in use, who uses it and where it is stored.
- [ ] Each key is moved into the secret manager and read from there by the service that needs it.
- [ ] Each key is rotated, and the old value is revoked.
- [ ] The date of the next rotation is recorded for each key.

title: Pilot dashboard: inspections per technician per day
body:
## Why
The pilot success criteria need numbers. A small dashboard that shows inspections per technician per day saves us from counting by hand.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A page for the pilot customer's workspace shows inspections per technician per day for the last four weeks.
- [ ] The page shows how many technicians were active in each week.
- [ ] Numbers can be exported as a CSV file.
notes: Not started. Wait for the pilot success criteria (#10) so we build the numbers that are agreed.

title: Larger tap targets on checklist rows
body:
## Why
Technicians wear gloves. Small tap targets on checklist rows cause wrong taps.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Every tappable part of a checklist row is at least 48 points high.
- [ ] The spacing between rows does not hide the next row on a small screen.
- [ ] A person wearing work gloves can tick ten rows in a row without a wrong tap.
